p:cNvPr.descr: A two-part structure, a and b, that illustrate gene silencing by RNA interference. In part a, two green lines that are partially lined with short vertical ticks, starting around the middle left point, form two loops toward the right end, one above the top line and one below the bottom line. At the right end, the two lines form a large circle. This is labeled Precursor. To the right of that is an arrow pointing down, labeled Dicer in blue. Below the arrow is a portion of the precursor, labeled stRNA. The left section of the previous structure that is not lined, and the right circular section, are cut off. Below that, another arrow points down to just the top part of the previous structure. Below that, an arrow pointing right and down, points to a structure labeled Silenced mRNA. This structure is a long green wavy line. Above it on the left side is the top structure previously described; on the right side is a wavy line that is connected to the bottom line by a series of short ticks. The bottom right segment is labeled AAA(A)(subscript n). Below that entire structure is an arrow pointing down and left to the text, “Degradation.” In part b, two green lines, one on top of the other, are connected by a series of green ticks in the middle. Two wavy lines cut the structure in half, so there are two distinct sections; this is labeled Duplex RNA. Below that is an arrow pointing down, labeled Dicer in blue. The arrow points down to a shorter, cross-section of the lines above, but this time, the top line is slightly pushed left, so that it is longer there, but shorter on the right, where the bottom line is longer. This is labeled siRNA. Below that is another arrow pointing down to the top part of the previous structure. Below it is an arrow pointing down and left to the silenced mRNA structure described in part a. Below that structure is an arrow pointing down and right to text that reads, “Translation inhibition.”
